applies_why: This judge text resolves D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14), a collision involving the challenger's own chain of sign-bounding verses, so it is the kind of chain collision K-C governs.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse — I weighed (1) that a judge may not use isolated verse or word-count points in the collision, versus (2) that noting a neutral word-count tie is permissible so long as the decision weighs the chains' footings; the judge's line acknowledges both chains' real footing and does not decide by the word-count.
why: The judge does not use the retired stating-verse test; it treats the chapter-bound verses as real support, notes C5's concession that Matthew 1:23's application stands, and treats the word-count as neutral, so it weighs the collision as underdetermined by chain footing rather than by a single contrary verse.
